evidence: Ov. A. A. 3.231–232: Aurea quae splendent ōrnātō signa theātrō, īnspice, contemnēs: brattea ligna tegit
terms.comment: A description of ours. Bractea is metal beaten thinner than a lāmina, gold leaf above all (Lewis & Short, after Isidore); Ovid’s gilded statues are wood under foil. Alūminium is the modern name of the metal (Morgan–Owens). No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for kitchen foil.

phrases.latin: Placentam bracteā alūminiī tege, nē exārēscat.
phrases.english: Cover the cake with foil so it doesn’t dry out.

phrases.latin: Aurea quae splendent ōrnātō signa theātrō, īnspice, contemnēs: brattea ligna tegit
phrases.english: Look closely at the golden statues that shine in the decorated theatre, and you’ll scorn them: it is foil covering wood
